instagram_caption:
What if gravity switched off for 10 seconds? 🌍

You might expect everyone to be flung into space. They wouldn't be. The ground under Venice is moving east at about 1,200 km/h as Earth spins, and gravity is what bends your path around with it. Switch gravity off and everything carries on in a straight line while the ground keeps curving away beneath it. In Venice that works out to only about 85 cm of drift in 10 seconds (and a little south too).

So everything gently floats: people, pigeons, gondolas, even blobs of canal water. Anyone who jumps just keeps going. Then gravity comes back, and everything drops about 85 cm at once. Venice gets very wet.

This is fiction. But astronauts on the ISS float every day, and gravity up there is still about 90% as strong as on the ground. They're weightless because they're falling around Earth at about 28,000 km/h.

Would you have held on? Did you spot him? 👀
